title: Leaders Who Make Fun of Themselves Build Trust and Comfort
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece argues that well-calibrated self-deprecation is a genuine leadership tool that builds trust and approachability rather than undermining authority. It explains the mechanism — self-deprecation disarms people, humanizes leaders, and is especially powerful for high-status leaders because it makes people around them feel more secure. The article draws a firm line, however, between light self-deprecation about minor flaws and disclosures of genuine doubt or incompetence, warning that crossing that line validates insecurities and damages credibility instead of building it. It closes by noting the practice must come from genuine confidence, not actual self-doubt, to land well.
points: Self-deprecation works because it disarms people and humanizes leaders, making them more relatable and trusted.
The effect is amplified for higher-status leaders specifically, since it makes people around them feel more secure and willing to speak candidly.
There's a hard line between light self-deprecation about minor flaws and genuine disclosures of doubt or incompetence — crossing it undermines credibility instead of building it.
The tactic only works when it originates from genuine confidence rather than actual self-doubt.
quotes: This is because self-deprecation disarms people and makes leaders more relatable and personable. People tend to trust leaders they find more likable.
By humorously acknowledging their own flaws, shortcomings, or mistakes, leaders show themselves to be human, which makes them more trustworthy.
Leaders should never attempt self-deprecation that goes too far by disclosing serious doubt or incompetence.

This perception is amplified for leaders of higher status. When others hold a leader in high regard or they have a significant title, position, or authority, self-deprecating remarks show them to be imperfect and serve to make people around them more secure.
Remember this: If you take yourself too seriously all of the time, others won’t.
